correctness.rationale: The induction handles every r>=1 and k_i>=4. A proper P3-closed S has complement T of induced minimum degree >=2r-1. After splitting along a longest cycle, an empty slice forces two full consecutive slices (and exactly those at minimum), while if all slices are nonempty, induction bounds each by 2|H|/L; equality requires tied largest factor and identical minimum lower-dimensional slices. The existence slabs have the required degree. Closed-set maximality gives the bootstrap statement. Finite independent enumeration independently checked 7,422,666 subsets on three 2D instances, plus 878 construction/random 3D-4D checks; computations do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Largest nonpercolating sets are a standard extremal robustness parameter for two-neighbor bootstrap percolation and P3 convexity. Establishing that every extremizer is a contiguous two-layer cut, identifying the controlling longest coordinate even when multiple lengths tie, and obtaining the exact count tK resolves a natural whole-family rigidity problem not given by the previously known numerical threshold. No unrelated ad hoc parameter or routine numerical increase is the objective; the classification states all optimal configurations for every dimension.
